search_scope.seat_change_semantics: Same-train seat changes are ticket boundaries while staying onboard one train run (no transfer window applies); train changes are validated transfers between different trains.

notes: These results are point-in-time availability checks, not booked tickets. RailRoute AI does not book tickets.
Every segment of every confirmed result explicitly reports confirmed availability (provider status AVAILABLE). RAC, waitlist, regret, unavailable, unknown and provider errors never qualify.

Journeys whose availability could not be fully verified are returned separately as unverified candidates (journey_status PARTIALLY_VERIFIED) and are never labelled confirmed. A provider error is never interpreted as an unavailable seat.

A same-train seat change means consecutive ticket segments on ONE train run while the passenger stays onboard: it is NOT a train transfer and no transfer buffer applies. Indian Railways ticketing rules for split journeys on the same train must be verified before relying on them.
Each train change happens at one interchange station with the exact same station code on both trains, inside the configurable minimum transfer buffer and maximum transfer wait.
Availability figures can be older than the check time (provider-side caching): each segment carries its provider last_updated_at and each journey reports the oldest one.

Fares are summed per segment and never estimated; when any segment fare is unknown the total fare is null and the affected segments are listed. Total waiting time counts train-change waits only (seat-change halts do not count).
Direct through trains are listed for reference only: their availability is NOT checked by this engine.

A mixed journey involves separate tickets on one or more trains; connection validity depends on the trains running to time. Verify railway rules and leave realistic buffers before relying on a connection.
